positions.as_written: Expect patellofemoral load to rise faster than tibiofemoral when running volume rises.
Read a foot strike change as moving load rather than removing it.
State whether a running figure came from a treadmill or from overground.
Foot strike retraining redistributes load from the knee to the ankle and Achilles, which is a trade rather than an improvement and should be described as one.
Offer cadence increase as a measurable per step load reduction rather than as a style correction.
Avoid presenting a modelled contact force as a measured one.

Weigh the patient's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations, because adherence to a volume plan decides the outcome more than the plan does.
